_comment: v0.16 #305 R1 'The Flood Ledger', the HELP (Skill) route -- and the owner of mill_flood_stack's LOCKED read. Fixture pre-banks heard_flood_ledger with the quest already in started_quests, so the run is exactly the route under test: the mill door's WEST approach (18,5), a plain interact on the flood stacks proving the SKILL_UNKNOWN + locked_toast arm, then press_field_skill [Basic Cleaning] on the same prop banking flood_prep_done and completing beat 1, then the worked-report row at the headman. Zero combat, and ledger_read_true asserted absent whole-run so the three routes are proven to bank distinct counters.

steps._comment: == THE MILL DOOR, WEST APPROACH == the fixture pre-banks heard_flood_ledger (the give beat is flood_ledger_talk's job), so this run opens at the door. (18,5) is the second legal approach to riverfarm_mill_door (19,5): free of blocked/entity/decor, and 'move right' faces the door without stepping. The exit always returns to (19,6), so entering west and leaving south is a real one-cell asymmetry -- pinned here on purpose.

== THE LOCKED READ (this script owns it) == mill_flood_stack carries skill_uses but NO requires_skill, so a plain interact falls through interactions.gd's requires_skill arm with an EMPTY skill id and takes use_skill's unknown branch: SKILL_UNKNOWN then the entity's locked_toast. There is no skill_hint_toast on this prop and there never can be -- that arm only fires from the requires_skill branch.

payload_contains.text: Sacks stacked low and a season coming for them. Lifting them above the flood line is work, and work is a Skill you either have or you don't.
Sacks stacked low and a season coming for them. Lifting them above the flood line is work, and work is a Skill you either have or you don't.

steps._comment: == THE HELP ROUTE == field-cast [Basic Cleaning] on the same prop from the same cell. press_field_skill resolves the bar slot by skill id and fails loudly if the skill is not on the bar; the fixture's loadout is AUTO, so every known field skill is slotted. The fixture holds basic_cleaning and NOT basic_cooking, so mill_flood_stack's second skill arm is deliberately unexercised here -- the plain-interact refusal above is this script's negative, and no ambiguity is left about which arm ran.

ORDER: record_accomplishment re-evaluates quests INLINE (wi_game.gd:1467), so the beat lands BEFORE use_skill emits its toast -- waiting on the toast first would move the since-cursor past this event.

payload_contains.text: [Basic Cleaning] — You clear the shed floor and stack every sack up off the boards. The count comes right the moment anyone can see all of it at once.
[Basic Cleaning] — You clear the shed floor and stack every sack up off the boards. The count comes right the moment anyone can see all of it at once.

steps._comment: The HELP route never fights either.
The three R1 routes bank DISTINCT counters: working the stacks must never bank the tally walk's.
== EXIT == mill_exit (6,8) -> riverfarm_village (19,6), one cell off the west approach this run entered by.
== REPORT == the headman has not been talked to in this run, so the first interact is his talk_pool line and the second opens riverfarm_headman.

Hub: heard_flood_ledger hides the start row, flood_prep_done opens the WORKED report. 0 'You said you don't truck with witches.', 1 'Just passing through.', 2 'Not much of a headman anymore, is there?', 3 "The flood work's done. The count came right in the doing.". Take 3.
flood_reported_worked: 0 'It counts better in daylight.' ends.
